intent.raw: create lean validators to mathematically (category theory) prove first that a DomainSpec spec is correct, then validate LLM-produced code as a functor (per CRAFT-INITIAL-DEFINITION.md) via a deterministic translator that lifts produced code (architecture patterns, tags, composability rules, graph data) into the DomainSpec language and checks it in Lean; LeanCodeValidator.lean likely already has some logic; research implementation/domainspec; do online research; use all subagent strategies
intent.objective: Produce a refined non-executed design + MVP-ready work pack for a two-stage categorical verification pipeline (Stage A spec-correctness in Lean; Stage B code-as-functor via a deterministic code->DomainSpec translator), grounded in the existing lean-code-validator and Craft's schema/data/functor/residue model.
intent.operator_sentence: refine: lean validators to prove the spec then validate LLM code as a functor via a deterministic translator into the DomainSpec language

items.label: Functorial Data Migration (Spivak)
items.description: Spec = small category, instance/code = Set-valued functor; validation = functor existence + Delta/Sigma/Pi migration laws. Closest to the existing sigmaValid edge-typing.

items.label: Functorial Semantics (Lawvere)
items.description: Spec = algebraic theory, code = product-preserving model functor; validation = structure preservation of operations/relations.

items.label: Spec-as-presheaf + Lan
items.description: Validator's own categorical roadmap (Quiver Meta, Spec-as-presheaf, Kan extension Lan for the open M6-graph theorem). Lan-faithful, not Full.

items.label: Abstraction/refinement functor
items.description: Code category abstracted upward to spec category by the deterministic translator; validation = the abstraction functor commutes with spec structure; residue = non-commuting part.
